The basic secret is the use of hydrocolloids. Primarily vegetable gums. Your feeling that a food is "rich" is typically a response to texture and mouthfeel from sauces saturated in fats or proteins. This same effect can be created through the use of hydrocolloids.

Here is a quick and easy way you can make faux cream: take almond milk (or skim, I'm diabetic so I avoid lactose, also almond milk is lower calorie), add xanthan gum at a ratio of 1/4tsp per cup. Blend and froth with an immersion blender (or toss it in a traditional blender).

You will find what you have now has the consistency of cream. DON'T add too much gum, a little goes a long way.

If you can find it, guar gum can be used to create a better lattice in the fluid with less added ingredients, and you can do some really wacky shit when combining with konnyaku flour or locust bean.

You will also find xanthan gum is a good anti-syneresis agent. Ever make homemade tomato sauce but you find it tends to "bleed" water when served? Xanthan gum improves colloidal suspension and emulsion, preventing this from occurring.

For cream of mushroom soup, prepare your faux cream in advance and substitute. Don't use a traditional thickeners like cornstarch and flour. Swap out the cream entirely, and cut back the fat and oils.

I start by pan frying mushrooms in 1/2 tbsp of sesame oil and add no more fat or oils when cooking. Add a Vidalia onion (chopped fine) and stir fry with the mushrooms.

2.5 cups of faux cream.

1.5 cup of chicken broth, ALSO thickened with xanthan gum in the same ratio and method.

2 tsp dill

1 tbsp paprika

1/2 tsp cayenne

1 tbsp soy sauce

2 tsp lemon juice

Salt and black pepper to taste

Once the mushrooms and onions have been cooked to release the aromatics, hit them with the spices, soy, and lemon juice.

Add the faux cream and "creamed" broth/stock. Heat till simmering, then back down the temperature and cook on medium for 5-10m.

We like adding spinach as well, and I usually grill some chicken breasts on the side for protein.

With almond milk (unsweetened) this is so low cal, you'll need the extra side of protein for sure.
